conviction_note: Two forces cancel. The ~$975M pre-tax GBT gain booked in Q3 (deal closed 2026-09-29, explicitly outside the $17.30-17.90 guide) gives management room to lift the REPORTED FY EPS guide, and the last time Amex raised its EPS guide in Q3 (2025-10-17) the stock rose +7.27%. Against that, underlying ex-gain EPS is tracking near the guide midpoint, management has said it will reinvest upside rather than let it reach EPS, and both 2026 prints where the guide was held fell -4.3%. The stock has also run up +5.9% in 20 days. So impact_sum is about -0.05, p_up is 48 and abs_move is 4.5 (option-implied event move 4.49%), giving a scaled -0.18. That number is effectively zero.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $20.12-20.13B, two sources agree: Zacks via Yahoo 2026-10-16 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/rising-expenses-affect-american-express-145000645.html) and Seeking Alpha watchlist (https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:a759662c6094b:0-american-express-q3-earnings-watchlist-revenue-card-spending-costs/). Q3 EPS (ex-GBT gain) is disputed: $4.47 Zacks (two downward revisions in the last 7 days, ESP -0.17%), $4.49 SA, $4.50 Public.com, $4.59 Benzinga. That is a ~2.7% spread, so every EPS-dependent size is capped small. Company guide (8-K 2026-07-24, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000004962/000000496226000318/q226exhibit991.htm): FY2026 revenue growth ~10%, EPS $17.30-17.90, which excludes the GBT gain. FY consensus EPS is ~$17.65 and FY revenue ~$79.47B (+10%), so the revenue consensus sits exactly on the guide. Reported Q3 EPS will include the ~$975M pre-tax GBT gain, so headline-versus-consensus comparisons will be distorted.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement was 10.82M shares, 2.70 days to cover, about 1.6% of shares outstanding (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/axp/shortinterest; the 2026-09-15 figure was 10.78M at 4.65 days). Not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is +0.65 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.25, event-implied move 4.49% against a 2.35% median own reaction. Spot 323.71 is +5.91% over 20 days and +3.14% over 5 days, 15.9% below the 52-week high. Reaction history: 6 of the last 7 prints fell, and the one rise (+7.27%, 2025-10-17) came on a Q3 EPS-guide raise.

findings.finding: Amex's ~30% GBTG stake sale closed on 2026-09-29, inside Q3. Amex's own 8-K put the pre-tax gain at ~$975M and proceeds at ~$1.5B, said the gain was 'not factored into the FY 2026 earnings guidance', and said it would invest a portion and return a portion to shareholders. That is roughly $1.0-1.1 of after-tax EPS against a $17.30-17.90 FY guide, so management has room to raise the REPORTED FY EPS guide even after spending part of it on marketing or technology.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS guide line: the 2025-10-17 Q3 print raised the EPS guide and the stock rose +7.27%. The 2026-04-23 and 2026-07-24 prints held the EPS guide and the stock fell -4.31% and -4.30% (baseline; HL/RTT coverage of 2026-07-24). No observed reaction to a gain-funded raise on this name in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The gain itself is public. What is not known is how much of it reaches the reported guide versus being spent. The Q2 call only said the guide excludes the gain and that upside is being reinvested. Published Q3 consensus ($4.47-4.59) is ex-gain, so headline EPS will print far above every aggregator number. If the market had priced a gain-funded guide raise, the skew would lean to calls and the stock would not sit 15.9% below its high at only 2.35% median reactions. Instead the skew is flat.
findings.independence: The GBTG 8-K ex-99.1 (separate filer) confirms the 2026-09-29 completion date. The Q2 2026 call summary (https://gloom.sh/stocks/axp/transcripts/q2-2026) confirms the gain was excluded from guidance and that management prefers to reinvest upside, which is the counterweight already reflected in the size.

findings.finding: Third-party card-spend data published after Amex last spoke supports Q3 billed business at or above Q2's +9% FX-adjusted pace. BofA Institute (2026-10-09) put September household card spending at +6.2% YoY, the third-strongest in four years. JPMorgan (reported ~2026-10-14) had card sales volume +10% YoY. Delta's 2026-10-09 release showed Amex remuneration +15% to $2.3B (+16% in Q2), driven by higher spend on Amex cards and new card acquisitions. Together these point to revenue landing at or slightly above the $20.13B (+9.3%) bar rather than at the +10% FY guide pace being missed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue line: Q2 2026 revenue +10% was a small miss against consensus and the stock fell (-4.3% per baseline). Q1 2026 revenue $18.91B beat and EPS $4.28 beat $4.03, and the stock still fell -4.31% on a held guide. This name sells reported-quarter beats unless the guide moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock is +5.9% over 20 days, rising alongside the bank prints. It is filed small because it is a proxy, not an Amex number. If it were unpriced, the Q3 revenue consensus would still sit below the guide pace. It sits at +9.3% against a ~+10% guide, a gap of only ~0.7%.
findings.independence: JPM card volume +10% (https://www.nordinvestimentos.com.br/blog/jpm-resultado-3t26/, 2026-10-14). Delta Q3 Amex remuneration +15% (https://beancount.io/blog/2026/10/10/delta-air-lines-q3-2026-earnings-analysis, Delta release and 10-Q dated 2026-10-09). These are three different counterparties, but all are proxies, and Delta's growth slowed one point from Q2's +16%.

findings.finding: Amex's own monthly 8-K (2026-10-15) shows Q3 US Consumer card net write-offs at 1.6% (principal only) and US Small Business at 2.3%. 30+ day delinquency ticked UP in September to 1.2% (from 1.1% in May-August) for Consumer and to 1.4% (from 1.3%) for Small Business. Over the same quarter, card peers reported improving credit: JPM card NCO 2.91% against 3.34% in Q2, COF consolidated NCO 2.73% against 3.23%. After Q2's $191M reserve release, a flat-to-small build is more likely than another release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not been the line Amex traded on in 2026. Q2 NWO was 2.0%, flat YoY, with a reserve release, and the stock still fell on expenses and the held guide. No baseline print in which credit drove the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a week, so mostly priced. The small residual is the provision line: consensus EPS revisions went down in the last week (Zacks). If the delinquency uptick were fully priced, the bar would sit lower. The 'Card balances' presentation differs from the 2025 'Card Member loans' tables (Q3 2025 consumer NWO 2.0%, delinquency 1.4% on $94.1B), so YoY reads in that document are not like for like and few will make them.
findings.independence: The prior month's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000004962/000000496226000345/axp-20260817.htm) shows May-July delinquency steady at 1.1%. It is from the same issuer and the same series, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: Ex-gain, Amex is tracking near the midpoint of its FY EPS guide, not above it. H1 2026 EPS was $8.81 ($4.28 + $4.53, +14%). Q3 consensus ~$4.47-4.59 implies Q4 must be ~$4.2-4.4 against $3.53 in Q4 2025 (+19-24%) to reach the ~$17.65 FY consensus, which already sits above the $17.60 midpoint. Management guided H2 marketing ~+10% YoY, pulled technology projects into H2, and has TheFork deal and integration costs coming. That makes an ex-gain raise unlikely, and on the two 2026 prints where the ex-gain guide was merely held, the stock fell ~4.3% each time.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Held EPS guide: -4.31% (2026-04-23) and -4.30% (2026-07-24). Raised EPS guide: +7.27% (2025-10-17). Of 7 baseline prints, only 1 rose.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY consensus of $17.65 already sits above the guide midpoint. If the market had priced a held ex-gain guide, that figure would sit at or below $17.60 and the stock would not have run up +5.9% over 20 days into the print. The gain gives management the option to present a 'raise', which may mask this. That is why this finding is sized small and kept separate from the gain finding.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 EPS of $3.53 and the FY2026 $17.30-17.90 guide come from Q4 coverage (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/american-express-reports-line-q4-124609892.html). Q1 2026 EPS of $4.28 comes from AP via WTOP (https://wtop.com/news/2026/04/american-express-q1-earnings-snapshot/). The Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000004962/000000496226000318/q226exhibit991.htm) confirms the held EPS guide and the reinvestment stance. These are different documents, combined in arithmetic.

findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar has drifted down into the print. Zacks recorded two downward revisions and no upward ones in the 7 days to 2026-10-16, consensus is at $4.47 (+8% YoY against +11% in Q2 and +14% in H1), and Amex beat in 3 of the last 4 quarters by an average 3.3%. A lowered bar makes an ex-gain beat more likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats were sold in 2026. Q1 beat $4.03 with $4.28 and the stock fell -4.31%. Q2 beat with $4.53 and the stock fell -4.30%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and mostly priced. It is filed because the bar is disputed ($4.47 vs $4.59). A beat on Zacks's number may be in line on Benzinga's.
findings.independence: Benzinga lists $4.59 and Public.com $4.50, which disagree with Zacks, so the drift is not corroborated.

findings.finding: Amex's second small-business co-brand portfolio (two sold, the Amazon portfolio named as one; both held for sale for over a year) was due to transfer out in Q3. Management guided ~1 point lower billed-business growth and ~2.5 points lower NII growth from Q4, with negligible pre-tax effect, already inside the FY guide. A mid-quarter transfer could shave Q3 billings optics slightly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction on this line. It was disclosed on the Q2 2026 call, after which the stock fell -4.3% on other items.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside the guided range and was pre-announced, so it is close to fully priced. The residual risk is a headline billed-business growth figure below the ~10% some will benchmark from Q2's 9.4%.
findings.independence: The monthly 8-Ks exclude held-for-sale balances (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000004962/000000496226000345/axp-20260817.htm). That is the same issuer, so not independent.

outside_window.finding: TheFork acquisition ($700M cash from Tripadvisor, announced 2026-06-15) is expected to close before end-2026. Its deal and integration costs land in H2 but are not dated inside this window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Amex remarks at the September 2026 Barclays Global Financial Services Conference: participation announced (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260817238136/en/American-Express-to-Participate-in-Barclays-Global-Financial-Services-Conference) but no transcript or coverage found

Status of a federal 10% credit-card APR cap in October 2026: only January 2026 coverage found
Capital One Q3 2026 domestic card purchase volume: the release table was truncated, so only consolidated NCO and delinquency were used
Company-specific AXP news in October 2026 beyond the earnings-call notice: none found

rejected_candidates.candidate: Amex Platinum fee $695 to $895, repriced at renewals from January 2026 and amortised over 12 months, so card-fee growth accelerates in Q3 and exits the year in the high teens
rejected_candidates.detail: This is company-guided card-fee acceleration from the Q2 call and is inside the revenue guide and consensus (Zacks average fee per card +12.3%). It merges into the spend and revenue finding and the guide finding.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Synchrony Q3 2026: record Q3 purchase volume, broad-based, EPS $2.68 vs $2.86
rejected_candidates.detail: A private-label, lower-income customer base. It adds nothing beyond the BofA/JPM spend series already filed in finding 2.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Brent near $99 and macro selloff on 2026-09-08 (Houthi strike, Canada tariffs) as a travel-spend headwind
rejected_candidates.detail: Delta's 2026-10-09 10-Q shows premium revenue +17.6% and Amex remuneration +15% in the same quarter, contradicting a Q3 travel-spend hit.

baseline_tension: Roughly neutral against a balanced skew (+0.65). The run-up (+5.9% over 20 days) and a FY consensus already above the guide midpoint cut against the positive gain finding, and the name's habit of selling prints (6 of 7 down) cuts against any long. The GBT gain is the one concrete reason this Q3 could repeat the 2025-10-17 guide-raise rally rather than the 2026 pattern.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): kept the GBT gain as lands_on one_off with a stated path to the reported guide, and trimmed it from +0.5 to +0.4 because the company said part will be reinvested
Rule 1 and rule 5 (reaction function, proxies): trimmed the card-spend read-through from +0.4 to +0.3; this name sold both 2026 beats and the evidence is counterparty proxies
Rule 6 (inside the guide): moved the co-brand portfolio transfer from -0.1 to -0.05 because it is inside the stated guide
Rule 6 (disputed bar, $4.47 vs $4.59): already capped every EPS-dependent size small; no further change
Rule 7: short interest checked at 1.6% of shares and 2.7 days to cover, not crowded, so the negative guidance finding is left at -0.6; p_up and abs_move unchanged
